beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A translation slides a figure, a reflection flips it, and a rotation turns it. All three keep its size and shape: they are rigid motions.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Coordinates give horizontal position, then vertical position. *A* is one right and two up from O, the origin at zero, zero.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: These sides measure four and three units; the square marks a right angle.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Translation slides every point the same way. Here, move two left and three down.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The result is the image; *A* prime names the image of *A*.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One minus two is negative one; two minus three is negative one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The arrow means goes to; every point gets these changes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each starts from the original. Translation can go any distance in any direction: up and right,

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: far left,

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: or straight down, without turning or flipping. Our example was two left and three down.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: From the original, reflection flips over the y-axis.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each point lands equally far across, perpendicular to this mirror.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: *A* stays two units high. Only x changes sign.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Changing y is a common slip: point *A* belongs across the mirror, at negative one, two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: From the original, any line can be the mirror: the x-axis,

do.text: Any line can be the mirror

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: a vertical line through three,

do.text: Any line can be the mirror

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: or the slanted line y equals x. Our example used the y-axis.

do.text: Any line can be the mirror

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: From the original, rotate about O through ninety degrees: a quarter turn counterclockwise, opposite to clock hands.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every point turns the same angle and keeps its distance from O.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Point *A* starts one right, two up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The turned route goes one up, two left, reaching *A* prime at negative two, one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This rule describes that quarter turn.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Starting from the original, rotation can turn any angle, in either direction: a half turn,

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: a small clockwise turn,

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: or three quarters counterclockwise.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And its center can be any point, even corner *A*. Our worked example was a quarter turn counterclockwise about O.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every length and angle stays unchanged. Same size and shape means congruent.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Translation slides; our example went two left and three down.

do.text: Translation: slide anywhere Example: 2 left, 3 down
Reflection: flip over any line Example: the y-axis
Rotation: any angle, any center Example: a quarter turn about O

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Reflection flips; our example used the y-axis. Rotation turns; our example was a quarter turn counterclockwise about O.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Translation, reflection, or rotation: same size, same shape. Every point follows the motion.
